interview.name: Rosa
interview.answer: The repair drive is now scheduled for Sunday at the community center.

reflections: Rosa is coordinating the repair drive and naturally becomes the organizer others rely on.
Bo and Cleo both respond with practical support, suggesting a cooperative group with clear role-sharing.
The interactions show Rosa building trust by assigning concrete tasks and thanking people directly.
Rosa is coordinating the repair drive and others are responding with concrete offers to help.
Cleo is taking a support role by tracking supplies and missing items, while Ira and Gus are available for in-person follow-up and materials.
The event location and time changed to Sunday at the community center, so coordination now centers on keeping the updated list and logistics clear.
Rosa is coordinating the repair drive and keeping everyone aligned on the latest schedule and supply list.
Gus, Cleo, and Mara each took on clear supporting roles: bringing tools, tracking missing supplies, and sorting donated items.
The group is working collaboratively with Rosa as the organizer, and the event has shifted to Sunday at the community center.
Rosa is the organizer who keeps the group aligned on time, place, and status updates.
Mara is taking ownership of sorting donated items and identifying repair work that needs parts or follow-up.
Uli and Kira are responsive participants who want clear confirmation and will help once the details are shared.
Rosa is the main organizer and point of contact, keeping the repair drive coordinated and sharing updates.
Kira, Quinn, and Oren are all supportive participants who are checking logistics, recruiting help, or offering to handle specific tasks.
The repair drive is stable and scheduled for Sunday at the community center, with attention still on final fixes and needed supplies.

events.text: Rosa: Absolutely — I’ll keep the repair drive organized and make sure everyone knows what’s needed.
